test.name: A hand-entered place is standardized by project_create, not typed by the agent
test.description: No FamilySearch ID: the agent builds a stub for Michael Brennan, born ~1850 in Boston, from the objective text alone. project_create standardizes every place in a hand-built tree, so the written fact's `standard_place` is the resolver's, not one the agent typed (provenance graded by test_standard_place_came_from_a_tool).

input.delegation:
init-project: Start a new project to research the origins of Michael Brennan, born about 1850 in Boston. No FamilySearch tree exists for him yet.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: No FamilySearch ID is given, so the agent should work from objective text and create a stub for Michael Brennan with an approximate birth (~1850) in Boston

`person_search` is available and returns no candidates. Falling back to objective-text stubs is correct only after the search runs — judge whether the search was attempted, since a run that never searched and a run that searched and found nothing reach the same tree.

Because 'Boston' is hand-entered (no person_read fixture returns it), project_create standardizes it itself: the stub birth fact's `standard_place` in the written tree is the tool's ('Boston, Suffolk, Massachusetts, United States'). The agent enters the place as the user stated it.
Tool Arguments: no place_search call is expected — the agent no longer holds that tool; project_create receives the place as stated

The agent should NOT write a `standard_place` of its own. project_create replaces any it supplies and reports that as a warning, so a supplied value is a Tool Arguments defect even though the written tree comes out right.
Should not pretend to have FamilySearch tree data — there is no person_read in this scenario
